discovery: The optical lattice clock and precision tests of fundamental physics with it

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Katori conceived the optical lattice clock, trapping neutral atoms at a 'magic' wavelength so that the clock transition is unperturbed by the confining light. This combines the low quantum projection noise of many atoms with the Lamb-Dicke confinement of trapped ions. Katori and Ye then brought the idea to maturity. Their clocks reached fractional uncertainties and instabilities at the 10^-18 to 10^-19 level, roughly a hundredfold better than cesium standards. This is a new measurement paradigm. These clocks have resolved the gravitational redshift over millimetre height differences within a single atomic sample and demonstrated relativistic geodesy with transportable clocks. They also place stringent limits on drifts of fundamental constants and on ultralight dark matter. They are driving the redefinition of the SI second and open quantum-enhanced, networked metrology. Few instruments have moved sensitivity so far so quickly or joined foundational physics so directly to practical application.
